hazard: Acid gas (H2S, CO2) and hot amine in amine regenerator C-4402
topEvent: Loss of containment from amine regenerator C-4402

barrierTypes.passive-hardware: Works without activation: design pressure, bunds, fireproofing, blast walls, drains
barrierTypes.active-hardware: Detect, decide, act automatically: PSV, SIS trip, ESD, deluge
barrierTypes.active-human: A person detects and acts: alarm with operator response
barrierTypes.procedural: Supports other barriers: inspection, procedures, training. Not a barrier on its own.

barriers.label: High pressure alarm PAH + operator response
High-high pressure trip PSHH, cuts hot oil to reboilers
High temperature alarm TAH + operator response
High-high temperature trip TSHH, cuts hot oil

threats.label: Loss of reflux due to level control failure on V-4406

barriers.label: Low level alarm LAL + operator response
Low-low level trip LSLL, trips reflux pumps P-4405A/B
Muster upwind, breathing apparatus, temporary refuge
Gas detection with ESD and ignition source isolation

removed.label: BLEVE
removed.reason: Regenerator runs at low pressure with aqueous amine. A BLEVE needs a pressurised liquid well above its boiling point. Not credible without justification.

escalationFactors.factor: Inspection or corrosion monitoring delayed or skipped
escalationFactors.control: Inspection backlog tracked as a leading KPI (API 754 Tier 4)

escalationFactors.factor: Loss of power to instrumented trips and alarms
escalationFactors.control: UPS on SIS, fail-safe trip design
Cooling system included in the critical equipment list

reclassified: Coursework listed alarm systems, manual shutdown procedures and muster points as passive barriers. Alarms are active-human. Procedures are procedural. Muster is a mitigation (emergency response) measure.
